title: The Merry Men, and Other Tales and Fables
summary: A collection of short fiction by Robert Louis Stevenson, gathering tales that blend Scottish gothic atmosphere, moral fable, and psychological horror. The title story follows a young man returning to his uncle's remote island farm of Aros, where a wrecked Spanish Armada galleon, rumored to hold treasure, and the treacherous tidal reefs called the Merry Men become entangled with his uncle's guilt and madness. "Will o' the Mill" traces a solitary man's quiet, contemplative life and his eventual acceptance of death. "Markheim" depicts a murderer's confrontation with a mysterious visitor on Christmas Eve who forces him to examine his conscience. "Thrawn Janet," written in Scots dialect, tells of a minister whose servant woman becomes possessed after a supposed pact with the Devil. "Olalla" is a gothic tale of a wounded soldier convalescing in a decaying Spanish household haunted by hereditary taint and doomed passion. "The Treasure of Franchard" is a lighter, ironic tale following a philosophical doctor, his wife, and an adopted orphan boy amid a discovered treasure and its complications. Together these pieces showcase Stevenson's range across horror, romance, and moral irony.
